name: MART (MLLM As ReTriever): Interactively Learning Multimodal Retrieval for Embodied Agents
venue: ICLR 2025 (preprint arXiv:2410.03450, submitted Oct 2024; DBLP conf/iclr/YueXK025)
authors_affiliation: Junpeng Yue (School of Computer Science, Peking University), Xinrun Xu (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Borje F. Karlsson (Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence / BAAI), Zongqing Lu (Peking University, corresponding author). Yue and Xu work as interns at BAAI.
code_url: https://github.com/PKU-RL/MART (linked in the paper as the official code release; as of access the repository is publicly visible but empty/unpopulated)
task_domain: Embodied agents / embodied household task execution (multimodal MLLM agents performing fine-grained control in 3D simulated home environments).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent setting: a retrieval-augmented MLLM agent (frozen GPT-4o policy) must complete long-horizon embodied tasks drawn from a task distribution by conditioning on one retrieved expert reference trajectory. Supervision comes from environment interaction: for training tasks, candidate expert trajectories are fed to the agent and their induced task success rates serve as effectiveness feedback. Train and test task distributions (and their memories) are disjoint, so evaluation measures generalization to unseen tasks/scenes. The agent outputs fine-grained control actions directly (not teleportation), with observations being egocentric images (plus natural-language feedback in AI2-THOR).
what_is_retrieved: Multimodal expert trajectories (sequences of task instruction + egocentric observation images + actions + environment feedback), used as in-context reference/grounding for the embodied MLLM agent. After Trajectory Abstraction these become condensed milestone summaries.
retrieval_grounding: Hybrid leaning toward a fixed/offline-induced episodic memory of expert trajectories. The retrievable store is built offline from planner-collected successful executions (separate train and test memories); it is not grown online during deployment. It is grounded in agent-environment experience (episodic trajectory memory) rather than a static document/KB corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Single-best (top-1) selection: the fine-tuned MLLM retriever scores candidate trajectories for effectiveness and the single highest-scoring trajectory is injected as the reference (one-shot, single-trajectory due to MLLM context-window limits). Not a completeness/minimal-set objective; effectively a precision-driven top-1 selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (effectiveness-based retrieval of an expert trajectory). Reuse: yes (retrieved trajectory used as in-context grounding for the agent). Revise: partial/implicit (Trajectory Abstraction condenses/re-represents trajectories into milestones and inferred rules conditioned on the current task, but the agent does not adapt the case into a new stored solution). Retain: no (memory is fixed offline; no write-back of new cases). Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=partial, Retain=no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as multimodal trajectory retrieval / memory retrieval with interactive preference learning; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or explicitly invoke case-based reasoning terminology, though it realizes Retrieve/Reuse mechanisms of CBR under another name.
retrieval_unit: Full multimodal expert trajectory (task instruction + observation/image sequence + action sequence + feedback), represented at retrieval/use time as a Trajectory Abstraction (a small set of key milestones, avg 3.13 milestones from avg 11.51 input steps).
index_source: Offline-induced growing-free memory: expert trajectories collected offline via a classical planner-based method (PDDL/FF-style planner) from successful task executions, then redundancy-filtered. Distinct training memory and testing memory are constructed offline (AI2-THOR: 170 train / 118 test sub-task trajectories; LEGENT: 40 train / 32 test trajectories). No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat memory pool of trajectories (no graph or hierarchy). Retrieval is performed by scoring each candidate trajectory in the (small) pool with the MLLM retriever rather than via a vector ANN index. For the Similarity+LLaVA and RAP baselines a flat embedding similarity index is used to pre-select top-K candidates.
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever / learned generative scorer: a fine-tuned MLLM (LLaVA-7B) augmented with a Bradley-Terry scalar score head acts as the retriever, directly scoring trajectory effectiveness for the current task+observation. (Baselines use dense embedding similarity; MART itself is the learned MLLM scorer.)
retriever_learning_signal: Downstream-task-effectiveness / interactive preference learning via a Bradley-Terry reward-modeling loss. For each training task, K candidate trajectories are fed to the agent; their induced task success rates produce a partial order; pairwise comparisons (C(K,2) pairs) form positive (higher success) / negative (lower success) preference pairs used to fine-tune the MLLM retriever's score head. This is effectiveness/interaction-based preference learning, not similarity-label contrastive training.
query_construction: The query is the current task instruction plus the current (initial) egocentric observation. The MLLM retriever takes (current task instruction l^c, current observation o_1^c, candidate trajectory abstraction A(tau_i^e)) plus a judging prompt, and outputs a scalar effectiveness score per candidate.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: a single retrieval is performed at the start of each (sub-)task using the initial observation and task instruction; the retrieved reference trajectory is then used throughout that (sub-)task.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per (sub-)task (retrieve once at the beginning of each task or sub-task, before execution). In AI2-THOR, tasks are decomposed into sub-tasks and retrieval occurs per sub-task.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered deterministically at the start of each task (or each sub-task after task decomposition in AI2-THOR); there is no uncertainty-, confidence-, or agent-initiated trigger.
reranking: MART itself functions as a one-stage effectiveness scorer/selector (no separate rerank stage in the full method). The Similarity+LLaVA (SL) baseline uses a two-stage retrieve-then-rank (embedding similarity top-K then plain LLaVA Yes/No scoring), and the Sim.+FTM ablation uses similarity retrieval then MART's fine-tuned model as a reranker; both underperform the unified MART.
retrieved_context_refinement: Trajectory Abstraction: a separate MLLM (GPT-4o, zero-shot) condenses each trajectory into key milestones (description + image + feedback + overarching actions between milestones), removing redundant/irrelevant steps and reducing token count while preserving task-relevant grounding (e.g., reduces a 73-step trajectory to 5 milestones; 13 transitions to 6 inferred rules). This is a decompose-then-distill/compression refinement applied before both retriever scoring and agent use.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs; the analogous step is Trajectory Abstraction which summarizes trajectories into milestone form before scoring and use).
index_content_separation: Partial: trajectories are stored in full but a lightweight Trajectory Abstraction (milestones) is what is fed to the retriever and agent, reducing context load. Not a formal index-then-content progressive-disclosure scheme; abstraction is the on-demand condensed representation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or external API protocol; memory is a static offline trajectory pool).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools / no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / in-context grounding: the single highest-scored expert trajectory abstraction is injected into the frozen MLLM agent's prompt as a reference to ground its fine-grained action planning for the current embodied (sub-)task.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-act with one-shot exemplar at plan time: one reference trajectory is retrieved per (sub-)task and used as a single in-context exemplar; in AI2-THOR long-horizon tasks are first decomposed into sub-tasks (ALFRED-style) and retrieval+execution proceed hierarchically per sub-task. The agent then directly outputs control actions over the finite horizon.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-(sub)task: retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of a whole task (LEGENT) or sub-task (AI2-THOR), not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-action within a rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted abstraction/condensation rather than explicit case adaptation: the retrieved trajectory is re-represented via GPT-4o Trajectory Abstraction (milestones / inferred implicit rules conditioned on the current task) and used as a verbatim in-context exemplar; the agent does not edit the case into a new solution. Effectively a distilled-exemplar reuse.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled milestone summary of a trajectory: each milestone contains a textual description, the corresponding key image, the corresponding feedback, and the overarching actions between milestones. Some cases yield an abstract set of inferred rules. (Surface form: condensed multimodal trajectory abstraction injected as in-context text+images.)
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled/condensed trajectory: between a raw trajectory and a reusable workflow. Trajectory Abstraction turns the raw multimodal trajectory into key milestones (and sometimes inferred implicit rules), i.e., a state-aware milestone/strategy representation rather than the raw step-by-step trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Two mechanisms: (1) the retriever is fine-tuned on interactive effectiveness preferences so it prioritizes trajectories that actually help (filtering out trajectories that are similar but ineffective/misleading, addressing the observed weak correlation between similarity and success); (2) Trajectory Abstraction removes redundant/distracting steps and irrelevant information before the trajectory is used, reducing distractor noise and context overflow.
memory_type: Episodic (a memory pool of expert trajectories / past task executions); no skill-library, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: False (no write-back): the expert trajectory memory is constructed offline via a planner and frozen; the agent does not store new experiences/cases during deployment. The only transformation is the offline/at-use Trajectory Abstraction of existing trajectories.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store is fixed after offline induction (separate train/test memories); it does not grow at test time.
write_back_trigger: Never (no test-time write-back). Memory entries are populated offline from planner-collected successful trajectories prior to training/evaluation.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only for the stored memory (only successful planner-collected trajectories are retained as expert references). However, the retriever's TRAINING signal is contrastive over effectiveness: trajectories yielding lower task success (relatively 'failed/less-effective' references) become negative items in Bradley-Terry preference pairs, so relative ineffectiveness is used as a learning signal (not stored as corrective rules).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at construction with offline dedup/redundancy filtering (about one-third of redundant AI2-THOR trajectories are filtered out). No post-write mutation, delta-update, or forgetting during deployment.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: case-selection is a LEARNED scorer (an MLLM fine-tuned with a Bradley-Terry preference/reward-modeling objective from interactive feedback) rather than fixed similarity top-k. It is a learned effectiveness ranker, but not an RL/value-based sequential retrieval policy (no soft Q-learning / M-MDP).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: AI2-THOR (with an ALFWorld+ALFRED-inspired custom embodied task setting, task decomposition into sub-tasks; 45 train tasks / 260 sub-tasks, 28 test tasks / 158 sub-tasks) and LEGENT ('Come Here' and 'Where Is' tasks, each One-room/Two-room; 40 train tasks, 32 test tasks).
benchmark_family: Embodied (AI2-THOR household manipulation/navigation, adapting ALFWorld/ALFRED; LEGENT embodied home navigation). RAP baseline references ALFWorld/WebShop/Franka-Kitchen/Meta-World, but MART's own evaluation is on AI2-THOR and LEGENT.
baselines: Plain-Agent (PA): GPT-4o agent with no reference trajectories/no memory. LLaVA-Plain (LP): pre-trained LLaVA, no head/no fine-tuning, scored via Yes/No token probability. Similarity+LLaVA (SL): embedding-similarity top-K retrieval then plain-LLaVA ranking (retrieve-then-rank). RAP (Kagaya et al., 2024): per-modality plain-similarity retrieval (most similar prior method).
key_metrics: Success Rate (SR), and in AI2-THOR also sub-task Success Rate (SR-Sub); Average Steps (AS), and sub-task Average Steps (AS-Sub) (lower is better; failed cases counted at the step limit). Each task tested 5 times.
headline_result: In AI2-THOR, MART achieves SR 0.40 vs best baseline 0.26 (LLaVA-Plain) -- a >10 percentage-point (over 50% relative) gain; SR-Sub 0.75 vs 0.69; AS 123.19 vs 144.18. In LEGENT, MART achieves SR 0.87 vs best baseline 0.75 (SL/RAP); AS 13.81 vs ~20.6. The paper summarizes MART as 'consistently surpasses baselines by over 10% across different environments.'
ablations: Table 4 ablates two components. (1) w/o Abstraction: removing Trajectory Abstraction drops AI2-THOR SR from 0.40 to 0.31 (9-pt drop) and LEGENT SR from 0.87 to 0.77. (2) Sim.+FTM: decomposing the unified MART into similarity-based retrieval + MART's fine-tuned model as a separate ranker drops AI2-THOR SR to 0.34 and LEGENT SR to 0.77, showing the unified effectiveness-scoring retriever outperforms a retrieve-then-rank pipeline; notably Sim.+FTM still beats SL and RAP, isolating the value of MART's learned trajectory-utility scoring. Case studies show on a 73-step task MART reaches 80% SR / 28 avg steps vs 40% / ~70-75 steps for similarity and no-memory baselines, and 80% SR vs 0% for others on an implicit-rule task.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task metrics (SR/SR-Sub, AS/AS-Sub) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are reported separately; the paper instead shows scatter plots of success rate vs embedding similarity vs effectiveness score to motivate the approach.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-oriented (task success rate). Average Steps gives a partial efficiency/process proxy, and case studies qualitatively examine milestone selection and trajectory quality, but there is no formal step-wise retrieval/planning accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is reported chiefly via Average Steps (MART reduces steps to success, e.g., AI2-THOR AS 123.19 vs 144-160 for baselines; LEGENT AS 13.81 vs ~20-25) and via token reduction from Trajectory Abstraction (avg 11.51 input steps condensed to avg 3.13 milestones), which lowers required context-window length. No explicit API-cost, latency, or retrieval-call-count accounting is given.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-1 selection (single best trajectory injected), motivated by the MLLM's limited context window (paper notes this restricts them to one-shot single-trajectory inputs). Trajectory Abstraction caps the token budget by reducing each trajectory to ~3 milestones. K candidate trajectories are sampled per training task to build preference pairs (K value [uncertain]).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Custom embodied task suites built on existing simulators rather than a new released benchmark: AI2-THOR setting integrates ALFWorld+ALFRED characteristics with task decomposition (45 train / 28 test tasks; 260 / 158 sub-tasks; memory 170 train / 118 test sub-task trajectories after redundancy filtering); LEGENT uses 'Come Here'/'Where Is' x One-room/Two-room (40 train / 32 test tasks; one trajectory per task in memory). Expert trajectories collected by a PDDL/FF-style planner; success verified by environment feedback / agent self-detection. Best system (MART) reaches only 0.40 full-task SR in AI2-THOR, signaling high task difficulty.
builds_on: LLaVA-7B (base MLLM retriever) with a Bradley-Terry (1952) reward-modeling preference loss / reward-model score head; GPT-4o as the agent policy and as the Trajectory Abstraction summarizer; AI2-THOR and LEGENT simulators; ALFWorld/ALFRED task design; classical PDDL/FF planner for expert trajectory collection; the general MLLM-agent-with-memory paradigm (Voyager, DEPS, Cradle, LLM-Planner, RAP).
contrasts_with: Similarity-based multimodal retrievers that select trajectories by surface-level text/image embedding similarity (the paper's central foil), the RAP method (Kagaya et al., 2024) of per-modality similarity retrieval, Similarity+LLaVA retrieve-then-rank, plain LLaVA scoring (LP), and memoryless agents (Plain-Agent / GPT-4o). Also contrasted with VLA models (PaLM-E, RT-2, Gato, VIMA) that train end-to-end policies without explicit memory.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience / trajectory retrieval for planning agents): an embodied, multimodal instance where the retriever itself is a learned effectiveness scorer (MLLM fine-tuned with interactive Bradley-Terry preferences) and retrieved trajectories are distilled (Trajectory Abstraction) before in-context reuse. Sits in the lineage moving from similarity-only memory retrieval to effectiveness/preference-learned, task-grounded trajectory retrieval for MLLM embodied agents.
